```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(modelsummary)

# All results come from code/05_analysis.R (run by run_all.R).
results_file <- here("output", "tables", "main_results.rds")
if (!file.exists(results_file))
  stop("output/tables/main_results.rds not found: run Rscript run_all.R ",
       "(or code/05_analysis.R) before knitting this paper.")
res <- readRDS(results_file)

# Number formatting for inline R (so no number is ever typed by hand).
num  <- function(x, digits = 3) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
pval <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else paste0("p = ", num(p, 3))

# Pieces of the confirmatory results used in the text.
h1 <- res$coefs |> filter(term == "conflict")
h2 <- res$coefs |> filter(term == "conflict:autocracy")
supported <- function(row) row$estimate > 0 & row$p_value < res$alpha
```

## Introduction

Governments restrict access to information when they feel threatened. Armed conflict is a prominent threat: it raises the stakes of controlling what citizens see and share, and it gives rulers a security rationale for doing so. This paper asks whether governments censor the internet more when armed conflict takes place on their territory, and whether this effect is stronger in autocracies, where rulers face fewer institutional and legal constraints on censorship.

## Data

We combine three sources. Internet censorship, regime type, and country identifiers come from the V-Dem Country-Year dataset (v16); armed conflict comes from the UCDP/PRIO Armed Conflict Dataset (version 26.1); GDP per capita and internet use come from the World Bank's World Development Indicators. The unit of analysis is the country-year.

The conflict indicator is 1 in a country-year if at least one UCDP/PRIO armed conflict with at least 25 battle-related deaths is located in the country, and 0 otherwise. V-Dem is the master frame: the panel contains exactly the country-years that V-Dem covers, `r num(res$n_panel, 0)` country-years in `r res$n_panel_countries` countries. The regression sample covers `r res$year_min`-`r res$year_max` and contains `r num(res$n_obs, 0)` country-years from `r res$n_countries` countries, after listwise deletion of `r num(res$n_dropped, 0)` country-years with missing values in the model variables. Armed conflict occurs in `r num(res$n_conflict_obs, 0)` of these country-years (`r num(100 * res$n_conflict_obs / res$n_obs, 1)`%), and `r num(100 * res$n_autocracy_obs / res$n_obs, 1)`% are autocracy-years.

## Research Design

We estimate a two-way fixed-effects model of censorship on conflict, its interaction with autocracy, and two controls, with country and year fixed effects and standard errors clustered by country. The specification, sample, and inference criteria are fixed in the pre-analysis plan (`pap/pre_analysis_plan.md`), which was committed before the data were downloaded.

## Results (confirmatory)

We estimate the model of the pre-analysis plan on `r num(res$n_obs, 0)` country-years from `r res$n_countries` countries. The table below reports the estimates and the figure shows the underlying means.

**H1.** In democracies (`autocracy` = 0), a conflict year is associated with a change in censorship of `r num(h1$estimate)` scale points (SE = `r num(h1$std_error)`, `r pval(h1$p_value)`, `r num((1 - res$alpha) * 100, 0)`% CI [`r num(h1$conf_low)`, `r num(h1$conf_high)`]). In a two-sided test at alpha = `r res$alpha`, H1 is **`r if (supported(h1)) "supported" else "not supported"`**.

**H2.** The interaction of conflict and autocracy is `r num(h2$estimate)` (SE = `r num(h2$std_error)`, `r pval(h2$p_value)`, `r num((1 - res$alpha) * 100, 0)`% CI [`r num(h2$conf_low)`, `r num(h2$conf_high)`]). H2 is **`r if (supported(h2)) "supported" else "not supported"`**. For interpretation, the implied conflict effect in autocracies (conflict plus interaction) is `r num(res$effect_autocracy$estimate)` (SE = `r num(res$effect_autocracy$std_error)`, `r pval(res$effect_autocracy$p_value)`); this is not a separate test.

**Deviations from the pre-analysis plan.** None: the model, sample, and inference criteria are those of the plan (git tag `pap-v1`).

```{r results-table}
modelsummary(list("Censorship" = res$model),
             coef_map = res$coef_map, gof_map = res$gof_map,
             statistic = res$statistic, fmt = res$fmt, stars = FALSE,
             title = "Confirmatory model: conflict and internet censorship",
             notes = "Higher censorship = more internet filtering. Standard errors clustered by country.")
```

```{r results-figure, out.width="100%", fig.alt="Mean internet censorship by year, for conflict and non-conflict country-years, in autocracies and democracies."}
knitr::include_graphics(here("output", "figures", "censorship_by_conflict.png"))
```

*The figure is descriptive: mean censorship by conflict status and regime type, with dot size showing the number of country-years behind each mean. It is not a test of the hypotheses.*

## Exploratory analyses

*No exploratory analyses have been run. Anything that is not in the pre-analysis plan (other censorship measures, controls, lags, subsamples) goes here, and is labeled as exploratory.*

## Reproducibility statement

All numbers, the table, and the figure in this paper are computed by code. To reproduce everything from the raw data, run `Rscript code/00_download_data.R` (downloads the raw data, and records their provenance in `data/raw/SOURCES.txt`) and then `Rscript run_all.R` from the project folder. The analysis was run with `r R.version.string` and fixest `r as.character(packageVersion("fixest"))`; the full session information is in the appendix. The confirmatory analysis is the one specified in `pap/pre_analysis_plan.md`, committed with the tag `pap-v1`.

AI use: the cleaning, merging, and analysis scripts and this document were drafted with a coding agent (Claude Code) and are recorded as co-authored in the git history.
